transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Start time: 08:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Alex Wu (Lighthouse Head of Platform), Maria Gonzalez (Lighthouse Security Lead), Derek Price (Lighthouse DevOps)

Summary (auto-gen): Security posture deep-dive focused on compliance artifacts and deployment options.

Topics: SOC2 scope, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency/retention, Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off. I see Alex, Maria, Derek — thanks. We'll keep this as a security posture discovery, try to cover your compliance questions and then map next steps.
[00:12] Alex: Great, thanks. We're evaluating Redwood for inference of PHI-adjacent data. Primary concerns are SOC 2 scope, whether you have ISO, and how we can deploy (we have a mix of public cloud and on-prem).
[00:24] Priya: Yep — quick intro from my side, I'm Priya on the infra team, I handle Dedicated and Private deployments and benchmarks. We'll be honest about what we support and typical architectures.
[00:34] Maria: Hi, Maria — security lead. For us, audit logs, SSO, RBAC, and KMS integration are blockers until we see proof. Also retention — we have a 7-year policy for some records so need clarity.
[00:46] Jordan: Totally understood. Quick question — are you expecting Redwood Hosted for POC or Dedicated/Private?
[00:52] Alex: Prefer Dedicated for the pilot for throughput predictability, but we may need Private/VPC or on-prem for production where PHI is in scope.
[01:00] Jordan: Good; that's a common pattern. We'll talk about how our Dedicated pools sit behind a VPC peering/PrivateLink and what data persists.
[01:10] Derek: Quick technical: how do you handle keys? We run KMS in our cloud and need to ensure customer-managed keys or HSM integration.
[01:19] Priya: Redwood supports BYOK via cloud KMS integrations — we can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own HSM in Private deployments. For Hosted we manage keys but there are enterprise options for dedicated key control.
[01:33] Maria: Can you clarify — for Hosted, does Redwood see unencrypted model input logs? What is redaction?
[01:41] Jordan: We have configurable logging. For Hosted we by default capture telemetry and aggregated metrics; raw transcripts can be disabled and redaction rules applied. For Dedicated and Private you control more of the persistence.
[01:53] Maria: Ok, need to review the exact retention config. Our legal team will require proof controls.
[01:58] Priya: We'll send the security questionnaire and SOC 2/ISO certs. For Dedicated we can also supply architecture diagrams showing no-persist modes and KV-cache controls.
[02:07] Alex: About SOC 2 — does it cover your entire platform or just the control plane?
[02:13] Jordan: Our current SOC 2 Type II covers the hosted control plane and multi-tenant API surface; we have scopes for Dedicated customers and separate artifacts for Private deployments. We'll share the report and the scope notes.
[02:24] Maria: Is there an SOC 3 or public summary?
[02:27] Jordan: We have an SOC 2 summary and letter we can share; SOC 3 not commonly published but we can provide an executive summary.
[02:33] Derek: Network-level — if we do Dedicated with VPC peering, is traffic egress encrypted and do you support PrivateLink?
[02:41] Priya: Yes, TLS in transit always. For Dedicated we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and customer-provided NATs. We'll include the network checklist.
[02:51] Alex: For Private/on-prem — how deep does the control plane go? Do you manage updates?
[02:56] Priya: Private has a customer-managed control plane option. We can do an air-gapped deployment but that requires an enterprise engagement; updates are via signed artifacts and can be on your schedule.
[03:07] Jordan: Maria — you mentioned RBAC — what are your requirements? Role levels, SCIM?
[03:12] Maria: We need SSO via SAML, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC so only the inference team can call model endpoints, while data scientists have read-only analytics. Also need audit trails for token usage.
[03:24] Priya: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with roles by default. Token-level audit logs are available; you can map roles to groups via SCIM.
[03:34] Derek: About audit logs — retention and access control? Logs need to be immutable for 90 days and archived for up to 7 years with WORM-like controls. Can Redwood meet that?
[03:45] Jordan: We support configurable retention. For Hosted we can retain logs compressed and export to customer S3. For Dedicated and Private you can push logs to your own logging infrastructure for long-term retention. WORM policies can be enforced on your storage side.
[04:00] Alex: Encryption at rest — who holds the key?
[04:03] Priya: For Hosted keys are managed by Redwood by default but enterprise customers can bring their own KMS keys. For Dedicated in a VPC you can either have Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed keys in your KMS. For Private/on-prem you control keys fully.
[04:18] Maria: HSM support? FIPS?
[04:21] Priya: We integrate with cloud HSM offerings and can support FIPS-validated modules in Private deployments as part of the enterprise package.
[04:30] Jordan: There's also the question of model artifacts and caching — the KV cache and model checkpoints.
[04:36] Alex: Are model weights stored persistently?
[04:39] Priya: Model weights are stored on managed storage; for Dedicated we can use customer-managed buckets or encrypted volumes. For Private deployments you manage the storage. Cache (KV cache) may be in-memory and ephemeral unless configured to persist.
[04:52] Maria: We'll want a diagram showing which artifacts persist and where.
[04:56] Jordan: We'll include that.
[05:00] [05:00] Maria: One more — compliance boundaries: if we route traffic through Europe for residency, do you have regionally isolated control planes?
[05:10] Jordan: We have region controls and can restrict routing to specific regions. For Private deployments, you can deploy fully in-region. We'll share the regional deployment doc.
[05:18] Derek: Logging formats — do you provide structured logs for tracing? OpenTelemetry?
[05:24] Priya: We support structured logs, request IDs, and have tracing hooks. We can push traces to your APM or export via OTLP in Dedicated/Private.
[05:35] Alex: I'm concerned about the multi-tenant risk surface for Hosted. If our dataset is sensitive, we probably need Dedicated or Private.
[05:44] Jordan: That's a reasonable posture. Many customers start on Dedicated for scale and then consider Private for PHI production. We can show typical SLA and isolation controls.
[05:54] Maria: Any third-party penetration testing?
[05:58] Jordan: Yes, annual pen tests, and we'll share summaries or attestations.
[06:03] [06:03] Alex: Ok can you talk about data deletion/retention API? We need programmatic purge for test data and a way to quarantine data used in evals.
[06:12] Priya: We have admin APIs to delete customer data and purge caches. For Hosted we have configurable retention windows and purge endpoints; Dedicated and Private give you full control so you can enforce retention policies your side.
[06:25] Maria: Is deletion immediate or eventually consistent across caches and backups?
[06:29] Priya: Usually eventual; we'll document the E2E process and expected timelines. For strict purge you should use Private with customer-managed storage.
[06:40] Derek: About token usage — can we rotate tokens frequently and link tokens to specific roles?
[06:46] Jordan: Yes, tokens can be scoped and rotated. We recommend short-lived tokens and the use of service identities for endpoints.
[06:54] [06:54] Alex: What about model evals — if we run evals with sensitive prompts, does Redwood persist prompts in eval stores?
[07:03] Priya: We can run evals in non-persistent mode; by default evals can be stored but we can configure to not persist or to encrypt and store in customer buckets.
[07:14] Maria: Any certifications beyond SOC2/ISO? FedRAMP? HIPAA BAAs?
[07:19] Jordan: We have HIPAA controls and can sign BAAs for Private deployments; Redwood is working toward more federal attestation but not yet FedRAMP. We'll include HIPAA artifacts and our security controls mapping.
[07:33] Alex: Timeline: we want a pilot in July. What's realistic?
[07:38] Jordan: If we move quickly we can spin up a Dedicated pilot in 4-6 weeks, run benchmarks, and then talk Private later.
[07:45] Maria: We'll need pricing and the security docs before legal signs off.
[07:49] Jordan: We'll send pricing bands for Hosted/Dedicated/Private plus a reference architecture.
[07:54] [07:54] Derek: On the Dedicated benchmark — can you simulate our traffic pattern (short bursty inference with long context ~2k tokens)?
[08:02] Priya: Yes, we'll include sequence-length-aware benchmarks and queueing/batching configs.
[08:10] Alex: Who is the single POC for Redwood on this?
[08:12] Jordan: I'll be your AE; Priya will lead the technical work.
[08:16] Maria: Jordan — please copy our compliance counsel on the SOC docs.
[08:19] Jordan: Will do.
[08:21] [08:21] Alex: Any blockers on our side? We need to confirm whether PHI is in scope for the pilot. If it is, we probably go Dedicated but with Private on roadmap.
[08:32] Maria: We'll confirm and share the data classification details.
[08:35] Jordan: Great. Quick note on audit logs again — we can provide a sample log schema and retention options.
[08:41] Priya: Also note our RBAC can integrate with Okta and other IdPs via SAML and SCIM; we support SCIM provisioning for groups.
[08:50] Derek: For network we'll need a peering test window and IP ranges.
[08:54] Priya: We'll include the network checklist and IP ranges in the follow-up.
[09:00] Jordan: Alright, let's recap next steps.
[09:03] Maria: Yeah, recap please.
[09:04] Jordan: Action items: we (Redwood) will send SOC2/ISO artifacts, security questionnaire, architecture diagrams for Dedicated and Private, network checklist, and pricing bands. Priya will draft the benchmark plan. Lighthouse will share data classification and retention policy and confirm PHI scope.
[09:23] Alex: Sounds good.
[09:25] Jordan: Any final questions?
[09:27] Maria: Not right now. We'll circle back after internal review.
[09:30] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to send the docs by Tuesday.
[09:34] Meeting end.
